meta.title: Throne — An app for agentic engineering
meta.description: Throne is an app for agentic engineering: the human sets direction and verifies, agents execute. The unit of work is the Intent — Throne pulls context, agent launch, and result verification around it. Local, a single binary.
meta.ogAlt: Throne — An app for agentic engineering

hero.title: An app for agentic engineering, built around the Intent
hero.subtitle: Agentic engineering is a discipline where the human sets direction and verifies while agents execute. The unit of work is the Intent: Throne pulls context, agent launch in the right mode, and result verification around it — and learns from every conversation. Local, a single binary.

theory.title: The productive AI work loop
theory.body: The interview unpacks the intent. Work delivers the result. The knowledge base captures context and feeds it back into the next pass — into the new interview and the new work.
theory.tagline: Throne closes this loop in one place: framing, agent launch, review of the result, and memory that feeds back into the next pass.

video.title: Throne in ten minutes
video.body: A short walkthrough: creating an Intent, launching the agent from the embedded terminal, and improving the result through patches.

features.title: Context under your control
features.subtitle: Throne gives the human one interface over intents, agent launch, and memory. Context no longer scatters across chats — it lives around the Intent.

items.title: Intent workspace
items.text: Every task lives as an Intent: a wording, history, links, questions, and work results. Context no longer scatters across chats.

items.title: Links between tasks
items.text: Connect Intents to each other: continuation, dependency, refinement, bug, fix. The agent sees a map of work, not an isolated request.

items.title: Launch the agent from Throne
items.text: Hit "Run agent" — Throne spins up a terminal right in the browser, hands over context and operational skills, and drives the session through hooks.

items.title: Memory and preferences
items.text: Your rules, style, and decisions are stored locally and applied automatically when the agent starts framing or a work session.

items.title: Dream retrospective
items.text: Ask your agent to review past conversations and propose a patch to your instructions. You accept or reject the change — memory improves transparently.

items.title: UX for the human
items.text: Throne shows what context a task has, which instructions the agent will receive, and what changed after the work. Memory management stays visible.

connect.title: Three steps to your first Intent
connect.intro: Throne runs locally: a single binary serves the UI, the API, and the database. No Docker, no cloud, no network auth.

install.title: Install with one command
install.description: macOS and Linux x64. The script downloads the latest release, installs the binary and the throne command, appends PATH, and starts the daemon. Re-running does a clean reinstall.

open.title: Open Throne
open.description: The daemon starts and opens the browser at http://localhost:5008. Manage it with the same command; update to the latest in one line.
open.snippet:
throne            # start daemon and browser
throne status     # port, pid, version
throne update     # update to latest

embedded.title: Run the agent
embedded.description: Create an Intent and hit "Run agent" — Throne spins up an agent terminal right in the UI, hands over context and operational skills, and drives the session through hooks. Host features — repositories, PR comments, open in VS Code — light up on their own as soon as the matching CLI is on PATH.

roadmap.title: Where Throne is heading
roadmap.intro: The core loop: brief the agent, give it context, verify the result, and keep useful takeaways for the next run. Each direction below strengthens one of these steps.

items.title: Easier verification
items.text: Diffs, change history, static analysis, diagrams. The goal — see faster what the agent got right and where another pass is needed.

items.title: Connecting work systems
items.text: Bug reports, task managers, messengers, and internal knowledge bases. Throne pulls in incoming context and turns it into an Intent.

items.title: Intermediate task memory
items.text: Steps, partial solutions, open questions, dependencies, and state across multiple agent passes.

items.title: Long-lived project context
items.text: Architectural decisions, repo rules, team conventions, and recurring patterns. The agent gets personal plus project-specific context.

items.title: Workspaces for teams
items.text: Roles, shared instructions, project memory, intent history, and access control. Throne becomes a team-level loop for working with agents.

contacts.title: Reach the author
contacts.body: Throne is run by a single author. Open channels — GitHub and Telegram.

footer.tagline: An app for agentic engineering, built around the Intent
